latin.699: §. III. SECUNDA CLASSIS Argumentorum PATRISTICA est, Argumentis primæ Classis parallela, ac proinde isti meritò succenturianda.
latin.700: Nam (1) de indignè Communicante omnium primo, Juda proditore, in vulgus notum est, Augustini judicium, in comparatione hujus cum communicante Petro, latum ac pronunciatum, quô Petrum & Judam, de uno quidem pane, ejusdémque panis partem, de eadem Dominica manu, accepisse, ait, Tractat. in Joh. 56. & Tom. post. collat. contr. Donatist.; interim tamen illum, seu Petrum, panem Dominum, hunc verò, seu Judam, panem duntaxat Domini, contra Dominum — Petrum, vitam (quia carnem Christi, quæ vivificat), Judam verò pœnam (quia impius, panem benedictum, qui judicium attrahit) accepisse. Tract. 59.
latin.701: Testimonium hoc Augustini adeò luculentum est, ut etiam Clarissimus Scultetus Hamburgensis eidem assurgat, dicens: Si Judas interfuit S. epulo, manducavit ille panem Domini ORE, non autem panem Dominum per fidem. Addens interim: Ipsi quoque Judæ, panis fuit communio corporis Christi (puta externa): Æque enim Judæ, ac reliquis Apostolis, dictum est à Christo: Non: Hoc, quod cum pane do, sed; Hoc, seu, hic panis, est corpus Christi. Discuss. Univers. Reform. §. 258. pag. 160.
latin.702: (2) De reliquis indignè communicantibus omnibus, eam solam ob causam, quòd in communione cum Christo haud sunt per fidem, sed in communione dæmoniorum ob impietatem, notum abunde est, non AUGUSTINI tantum judicium, quando Lib. 21. de Civitate DEI Cap. 25. Non dicendum, inquit, eum manducare corpus Christi, qui in corpore non est Christi. Et paulò post: Nec isti dicendi sunt manducare corpus Christi, qui nec in membris sunt computandi Christi: Non enim possunt simul esse membra Christi, & Meretricis. Et rursus, simile quid Tract. 26. in Joh.; Sed & S. HIERONYMI in cap. 66. Esaiæ: Qui non Sancti sunt, & Corpore & Spiritu, nec carnem Christi edunt, nec sanguinem ejus bibunt, de quibus dictum: Qui manducat carnem meam & bibit sanguinem meum, habet vitam æternam. Et adhuc paulò antiquioris Scriptoris, ORIGINIS nempe, Comm. in Matth. cap. 15. Christus, inquit, verus cibus est, quicunque illum edit, vivet in æternum, de quo impius nullus edere potest. Nam si possibile esset quemquam in impietate persistentem, verbum caro factum edere, nunquam scriptum foret: Quicunque edit hunc panem, vivet in æternum.
latin.703: Nec hîc tacendus PASCHASIUS RHADEBERTUS, quem nonnulli Theologorum Lutheranorum, præcipuum sententiæ suæ de Orali corporis Christi manducatione citra dentium lacerationem, Fautorem faciunt, indignè communicantes i. e. impios à participatione corporis Christi disertè & plus semel excipiens. Vide suprà Annot. 2. §. 5.
latin.704: (3) De iisdem omnibus, seu indignè communicantibus, qui per malitiam suam & improbitatem extra communionem Christi positi, nihilominus mensæ Domini communicant, eos sibi æternum exitium comedere, & Augustini, & multorum aliorum Patrum testimonia exstant. Ita enim denuo Augustinus: Ille qui non in Christo manet, & Christus in illo, non edit spiritualiter carnem ejus & sanguinem ejus bibit, etiamsi visibiliter & carnaliter dentibus premat, (non, corpus Christi & sanguinem) sed Sacramentum Corporis & Sang. Christi, seu potius edit & bibit Sacramentum tantæ rei, in condemnationem. Cui prælusit Zeno Veronensis, Origini coævus: Verendi causa est, ait, eum, in quo Diabolus habitat, non edere carnem Domini, nec bibere ejus Sanguinem, etiamsi videatur cum fidelibus communicare: Quandoquidem verba Domini ita habent: Qui manducat carnem meam & bibit Sanguinem meum, ille in me manet & ego in ipso.
latin.705: Utrique verò adstipulatus Bernardus, Epist. ad fratres de Monte: Sacramentum sicut ad vitam accipit dignus, sic ad judicium & mortem suam indignus. Rem enim Sacramenti nemo percipit, nisi dignus & Idoneus. Sacramentum enim sine re mors est; Res autem sacramenti, etiam præter sacramentum, sumenti, est vita æterna.

pass_a.699: §. III. The SECOND CLASS of Arguments is PATRISTIC, parallel to the Arguments of the first Class, and therefore deservedly to be enlisted under it.
pass_a.700: For (1) concerning the first of all who communicate unworthily, Judas the betrayer, Augustine’s judgment is commonly known, pronounced in comparing him with communicating Peter — that Peter and Judas received from one bread, a part of the same bread, from the same Lord’s hand (Tract. in Joh. 56; and Tom. post. collat. against the Donatists); yet meanwhile that one, Peter, received the bread the Lord, but this one, Judas, only the bread of the Lord against the Lord — Peter, life (because Christ’s flesh which vivifies), but Judas, penalty (because impious, the blessed bread which draws judgment). Tract. 59.
pass_a.701: This testimony of Augustine is so lucid that even the most distinguished Scultetus of Hamburg rises to it, saying: If Judas was present at the sacred feast, he ate the bread of the Lord WITH THE MOUTH, but not the bread the Lord by faith. Adding meanwhile: For Judas too the bread was communion of Christ’s body (namely external): For equally to Judas as to the remaining Apostles it was said by Christ — not: This which I give with the bread, but: This, or, this bread, is Christ’s body. Discuss. Univers. Reform. §. 258. p. 160.
pass_a.702: (2) Concerning all the remaining who communicate unworthily, for this sole cause that they are not in communion with Christ by faith but in communion of demons because of impiety, Augustine’s judgment is abundantly known — not only his — when in City of God 21.25 he says: It is not to be said that he eats Christ’s body who is not in Christ’s body. And a little later: Nor are those to be said to eat Christ’s body who are not to be counted in Christ’s members: For they cannot at once be members of Christ and of a Harlot. And again likewise Tract. 26 on John; and also St. JEROME on Isaiah 66: Those who are not Holy in Body and Spirit neither eat Christ’s flesh nor drink his blood, of whom it is said: Who eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life. And of a still somewhat older Writer, ORIGEN, Comm. on Matt. 15: Christ, he says, is true food; whoever eats him will live forever, of which no impious person can eat. For if it were possible that anyone persisting in impiety eat the Word made flesh, it would never have been written: Whoever eats this bread will live forever.
pass_a.703: Nor here is PASCHASIUS RADBERTUS to be passed in silence — whom some Lutheran theologians make the chief Patron of their opinion of Oral eating of Christ’s body without tearing by the teeth — expressly and more than once excepting those who communicate unworthily, i.e. the impious, from participation of Christ’s body. See above Annot. 2. §. 5.
pass_a.704: (3) Concerning all the same — those communicating unworthily who by their malice and wickedness are placed outside Christ’s communion, yet nevertheless communicate at the Lord’s table — that they eat eternal ruin to themselves, testimonies of Augustine and of many other Fathers stand. Thus again Augustine: He who does not abide in Christ, and Christ in him, does not eat his flesh spiritually and drink his blood, even if visibly and carnally he presses with the teeth — not Christ’s body and blood — but the Sacrament of Christ’s Body and Blood, or rather eats and drinks the Sacrament of so great a thing unto condemnation. Whom Zeno of Verona, Origen’s contemporary, foreshadowed: There is cause to fear, he says, that he in whom the Devil dwells does not eat the Lord’s flesh nor drink his Blood, even if he seem to communicate with the faithful — since the Lord’s words so hold: Who eats my flesh and drinks my Blood, he abides in me and I in him.
pass_a.705: And Bernard assents to both, Epistle to the brothers of the Mount: The Sacrament, as the worthy receives unto life, so the unworthy unto judgment and his death. For no one perceives the Thing of the Sacrament unless worthy and Fit. For the Sacrament without the Thing is death; but the Thing of the sacrament, even apart from the sacrament, for the one taking it, is eternal life.

699: §.III opens the second class of arguments: patristic.
It runs parallel to Class I and is enlisted under it.
700: (1) On Judas, first unworthy communicant: Augustine compares him with Peter — same bread, same Lord’s hand (Tract. Joh. 56; against the Donatists).
Yet Peter received the bread the Lord (life — vivifying flesh); Judas only the bread of the Lord against the Lord (penalty — blessed bread that draws judgment). Tract. 59.
701: Scultetus of Hamburg rises to that Augustine: if Judas was at the feast, he ate the Lord’s bread with the mouth, not the Lord-bread by faith.
Even for Judas the bread was external communion of Christ’s body — Christ said to him as to the rest, “this bread is my body” (Discuss. Univers. Reform. §.258).
702: (2) For all other unworthy communicants — not in Christ by faith but in demon-communion by impiety — Augustine (Civ. Dei 21.25): one not in Christ’s body does not eat Christ’s body; members of Christ and of a harlot cannot be the same (also Tract. Joh. 26).

Jerome (Isa. 66): the unholy in body and spirit neither eat the flesh nor drink the blood that gives eternal life. Origen (Matt. 15): Christ is true food no impious can eat — else “whoever eats this bread lives forever” would be false.
703: Paschasius Radbertus — whom some Lutherans claim as chief patron of Oral eating without teeth-tearing — must not be skipped.
He expressly and repeatedly excepts the unworthy (the impious) from participation of Christ’s body (see Annot. 2 §.5).
704: (3) Those outside Christ’s communion by malice who still take the Lord’s table eat eternal ruin to themselves — so Augustine and many Fathers.

Augustine: without abiding in Christ they do not eat spiritually, even if teeth press the sacrament unto condemnation. Zeno of Verona: the one in whom the Devil dwells does not eat the Lord’s flesh, though he seem to communicate with the faithful (Jn 6).
705: Bernard agrees: the worthy receive the sacrament unto life; the unworthy unto judgment and death.

No one perceives the Thing (res) of the sacrament unless worthy and fit — sacrament without the Thing is death; the Thing, even apart from the sacrament, is eternal life. Stop §.III before §.IV (patristic metonymy).
